q: A man gets a simple interest on Rs. 1000 on a certain principal at the rate of 5 p.c.p.a. in 4 years. What compound interest will the man get on twice the principal in 2 years at the same rate ?

The formula for simple interest is: Simple Interest = (Principal × Rate × Time) / 100 Solving for the Principal: In this problem, we know the simple interest (Rs. 1000), the rate (5% per year), and the time (4 years). We can use the simple interest formula to find the principal: 1000 = (Principal × 5 × 4) / 100 Solving for Principal, we get: Principal = Rs. 5000 Understanding Compound Interest: Compound interest is calculated on the principal amount plus accumulated interest from previous periods. It grows faster than simple interest. The formula for compound interest is a bit more complex, but we can break it down step-by-step. Calculating Compound Interest: The question asks for the compound interest on twice the principal (2 × Rs. 5000 = Rs. 10000) for 2 years at 5% interest. Year 1: Interest = (10000 × 5 × 1) / 100 = Rs. 500 Amount at the end of Year 1 = 10000 + 500 = Rs. 10500 Year 2: Interest = (10500 × 5 × 1) / 100 = Rs. 525 Total compound interest over 2 years = 500 + 525 = Rs. 1025 Therefore, the correct answer is B: Rs. 1025 (Note: There's a discrepancy in the provided options. q: A man invests Rs. 5000 for 3 years at 5% p.a. compound interest reckoned yearly. Income tax at the rate of 20% on the interest earned is deducted at the end of each year. Find the amount at the end of the third year = ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{C}}{\text{.I}}{\text{. earned during }}{{\text{1}}^{{\text{st}}}}{\text{ year}} \\ & {\text{= }}\,{\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left[ {5000\left( {1 + \frac{5}{{100}}} \right) - 5000} \right]{\text{ }} \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}\left( {5250 - 5000} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. 250}} \\ & {\text{Amount after }}{{\text{1}}^{{\text{st}}}}{\text{ year}} \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}\left( {5250 - 20\% {\text{ of }}250} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {5250 - 50} \right){\text{ }} \\ & {\text{= }}\,{\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\,{\text{5200 }} \\ & {\text{C}}{\text{.I}}{\text{. earned during }}{{\text{2}}^{{\text{nd}}}}{\text{ year}} \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left[ {5200\left( {1 + \frac{5}{{100}}} \right) - 5200} \right]{\text{ }} \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}\left( {5460 - 5200} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.260 }} \\ & {\text{Amount after }}{{\text{2}}^{{\text{nd}}}}{\text{ year}} \\ & {\text{= Rs}}{\text{. }}\left( {5460 - 20\% {\text{ of }}260} \right) \\ & {\text{= Rs}}{\text{. }}\left( {5460 - 52} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\,{\text{5408 }} \\ & {\text{C}}{\text{.I}}{\text{. earned during }}{{\text{3}}^{{\text{rd}}}}{\text{ year}} \\ & {\text{= Rs}}{\text{. }}\left[ {5408\left( {1 + \frac{5}{{100}}} \right) - 5408} \right] \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}\left( {5678.40 - 5408} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\,{\text{270}}{\text{.40 }} \\ & {\text{Amount after }}{{\text{3}}^{{\text{rd}}}}{\text{ year}} \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}\left( {5678.40 - 20\% \,{\text{of }}270.40} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}\left( {5678.40 - 54.08} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. 5624}}{\text{.32}} \end{aligned}$$

q: At a certain rate per annum, the simple interest on a sum of money for one year is Rs. 260 and the compound interest on the same sum for two years is Rs. 540.80. The rate of interest per annum is = ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{SI for 1 year}} \\ & {\text{ = Rs 260}} \\ & {\text{SI for 2 year}} \\ & {\text{ = 260}} \times {\text{2}} \\ & {\text{ = Rs}}{\text{. 520 }} \\ & {\text{Difference in (CI}} - {\text{SI)}} \\ & \left( {540.80 - 520} \right){\text{ = Rs 20}}{\text{.8}} \\ & {\text{Required rate \% }} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{20.8}}{{260}} \times {\text{100}} \\ & {\text{ = 8\% }} \end{aligned}$$

q: The simple interest on a sum of money at 4% per annum for 2 years is Rs 80. The compound interest on the same sum for the same period is = ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Rate }}\% {\text{ = 4}}\% \\ & {\text{Time (}}{{\text{t}}_1}) = 2\,{\text{years}} \\ & {\text{SI for 2 years}} \\ & {\text{ = 4}} \times {\text{2 = 8}}\% \\ & {\text{CI for 2 years}} \\ & {\text{ = 4 + 4 + }}\frac{{4 \times 4}}{{100}} \\ & = 8.16\% \\ & \operatorname{Required} \,CI \\ & = \frac{{80}}{8} \times 8.16 \\ & = Rs.\,81.60 \end{aligned}$$

q: The compound interest on Rs. 30000 at 7% per annum is Rs. 4347. The period (in years) is = ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Amount = Rs}}{\text{. }}\left( {30000 - 4347} \right) \\ & {\text{Amount = Rs}}{\text{. }} 34347 \\ & {\text{Let the time be }}n{\text{ years}} \\ & {\text{Then,}} \\ & {\text{30000}}{\left( {1 + \frac{7}{{100}}} \right)^n} = 34347 \\ & \Leftrightarrow {\left( {\frac{{107}}{{100}}} \right)^n} = \frac{{34347}}{{30000}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow {\left( {\frac{{107}}{{100}}} \right)^n} = \frac{{11449}}{{10000}} = {\left( {\frac{{107}}{{100}}} \right)^2} \\ & \therefore n = {\text{ 2 years}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The compound interest on a certain sum of money at 5% per annum for 2 years is Rs 246. The simple interest on the same sum for 3 years at 6% per annum is = ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Effective rate of CI for 2 years}} \\ & {\text{= 5 + 5 + }}\frac{{5 \times 5}}{{100}} \\ & = 10.25\% \\ & {\text{Effective rate of SI for 3 years}} \\ & {\text{= 6}} \times {\text{3 = 18\% }} \\ & {\text{According to question}} \\ & {\text{Required SI}} \\ & {\text{= }}\frac{{246}}{{10.25}} \times 18 \\ & = {\text{Rs. 432}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The difference between compound and simple interest on a certain sum for 3 years at 5% per annum is Rs. 122. The sum is = ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow P\left[ {{{\left( {\frac{{21}}{{20}}} \right)}^3} - 1 - \frac{3}{{20}}} \right] = 122 \\ & \Rightarrow P\left[ {\frac{{{{21}^3} - {{20}^3} - 3 \times {{20}^2}}}{{{{20}^3}}}} \right] = 122 \\ & \Rightarrow P\left[ {\frac{{9261 - 8000 - 1200}}{{8000}}} \right] = 122 \\ & \Rightarrow P \times \frac{{61}}{{8000}} = 122 \\ & \Rightarrow P = \frac{{8000 \times 122}}{{61}} \\ & \Rightarrow P = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\,16000 \end{aligned}$$

q: Rs.2000 amounts to Rs. 2226.05 in 2 years at compound interest. What will be the rate of interest ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let the rate be R}}\% {\text{ p}}{\text{.a}}{\text{.}} \\ & {\text{Then,}} \\ & {\text{2000}}{\left( {1 + \frac{{\text{R}}}{{100}}} \right)^2} = 2226.05 \\ & \Rightarrow {\left( {1 + \frac{{\text{R}}}{{100}}} \right)^2} = \frac{{222605}}{{200000}} \\ & \, \Rightarrow {\left( {1 + \frac{{\text{R}}}{{100}}} \right)^2} = \frac{{44521}}{{40000}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\left( {1 + \frac{{\text{R}}}{{100}}} \right)^2} = {\left( {\frac{{221}}{{200}}} \right)^2} \\ & \Rightarrow 1 + \frac{{\text{R}}}{{100}} = \frac{{211}}{{200}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{\text{R}}}{{100}} = \frac{{11}}{{200}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{R}} = \frac{{11}}{2}\% \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{R}} = 5.5\% \end{aligned}$$

q: A certain some of money and Rs. 2420 in 2 years and Rs. 2662 in 3 years at same rate of compound interest, compounded annually. The rate of interest per annum is = ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Amount after three years}} \\ & {\text{ = Rs. 2662}} \\ & {\text{Amount after two years}} \\ & {\text{ = Rs. 2420}} \\ & {\text{Net interest earned in the }}{{\text{3}}^{{\text{rd}}}}{\text{ year}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\,{\text{2662}} - {\text{2420}} \\ & {\text{ = Rs}}{\text{. 242}} \\ & {\text{Rate of interest (r)}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{242}}{{2420}} \times {\text{100 = 10\% }} \end{aligned}$$ (∴ 2 nd year's amount is principal for 3 rd year)

q: Kamal took Rs. 6800 as a loan which along with interest is to be repaid in two equal annual installment. If the rate of interest is $$12\frac{1}{2}$$ % compounded annually, then the value of each installment is = ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Rate of interest}} \\ & {\text{r}} = {\text{12}}\frac{1}{2}\% = \frac{1}{8} \end{aligned}$$ Year Principal Installment ⇒ I 8 ×9 → 9 ×9 ......(i) ⇒ II 64 → 81 ......(ii) Since, installment is equal hence multiply equation (i) by 9 ⇒ Total principal = 72 + 64 = 136 units 136 units → 6800 1 units → 50 81 units → 4050 ⇒ Each installment = Rs. 4050

q: A man invests Rs 4000 for 3 years at compound interest. After one year the money amounts to Rs. 4320. What will be the amount (to the nearest rupee) due at the end of 3 years ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Le the rate be R }}\% {\text{ p}}{\text{.a}}{\text{.}} \\ & {\text{Then,}} \\ & {\text{4000}}\left( {1 + \frac{{{\text{R }}}}{{100}}} \right) = 4320 \\ & \Rightarrow 1 + \frac{{{\text{R }}}}{{100}} = \frac{{4320}}{{4000}} = \frac{{108}}{{100}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{{\text{R }}}}{{100}} = \frac{8}{{100}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{R }} = 8 \\ & \therefore {\text{Amount after 3 yeras}} \\ & {\text{ = Rs}}{\text{. }}\left[ {4000 + {{\left( {1 + \frac{8}{{100}}} \right)}^3}} \right] \\ & {\text{ = Rs}}{\text{. }}\left( {4000 \times \frac{{27}}{{25}} \times \frac{{27}}{{25}} \times \frac{{27}}{{25}}} \right) \\ & {\text{ = Rs}}{\text{. }}\left( {\frac{{629856}}{{125}}} \right) \\ & {\text{ = Rs}}{\text{. }}5038.848 \approx 5039 \end{aligned}$$

q: A sum of Rs. 13360 was borrowed at $${\text{8}}\frac{3}{4}$$ % per annum compound interest and paid back in two years in two equal annual installments. What was the amount of each installment ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Rate of interest (r)}} \\ & {\text{ = 8}}\frac{3}{4}\% = \frac{7}{{80}} = \frac{{87 \to {\text{ Installment}}}}{{80 \to {\text{Principal}}}} \end{aligned}$$ ⇒ I 80 ×87 → 87 ×87 ......(i) ⇒ II 6400 → 7569 ......(ii) Since, installment is equal hence multiply equation (i) by 87 ⇒ Total principal = 6960 + 6400 = 13360 ⇒ 13360 units = Rs. 13360 ⇒ 1 units = Rs. 1 ⇒ 7569 units = Rs. 7569 ∴ Each installment = Rs. 7569

q: An amount of Rs. 10000 becomes Rs. 14641 in 2 years if the interest is compounded half yearly. What is the rate of compound interest p.c.p.a. ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let the rate be R\% p}}{\text{.a}}{\text{. }} \\ & {\text{Then,}} \\ & {\text{10000}}{\left( {1 + \frac{{\text{R}}}{{2 \times 100}}} \right)^4} = 14641 \\ & \Rightarrow {\left( {1 + \frac{{\text{R}}}{{200}}} \right)^4} = \frac{{14641}}{{10000}} = {\left( {\frac{{11}}{{10}}} \right)^4} \\ & \Rightarrow 1 + \frac{{\text{R}}}{{200}} = \frac{{11}}{{10}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{\text{R}}}{{200}} = \frac{1}{{10}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{R}} = {\text{20\% }} \end{aligned}$$

q: In how many years will a sum of Rs. 800 at 10% per annum compounded semi annually become Rs. 926.10?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let the time be }}n{\text{ year}} \\ & {\text{Then,}} \\ & {\text{800}} \times {\left( {1 + \frac{5}{{100}}} \right)^{2n}} = 926.10 \\ & \Leftrightarrow {\left( {1 + \frac{5}{{100}}} \right)^{2n}} = \frac{{9261}}{{8000}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow {\left( {\frac{{21}}{{20}}} \right)^{2n}} = {\left( {\frac{{21}}{{20}}} \right)^3} \\ & \Leftrightarrow 2n = 3 \\ & \Leftrightarrow n = \frac{3}{2} \\ & \therefore n = 1\frac{1}{2}{\text{years}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A loan of Rs. 12300 at 5% per annum compound interest, is to be repaid in two equal annual installments at the end of every year. Find the amount of each installment ?
s: $$5\% = \frac{1}{{20}} = \frac{{21 \to {\text{ Installment}}}}{{20 \to {\text{ Principal}}}}$$ Year Principal Installment ⇒ I 20 ×21 → 21 ×21 ......(i) ⇒ II 400→ 441 .....(ii) Since, installment is equal, hence multiply equation (i) by 21 ⇒ Total principal = 420 + 400 = 820 ⇒ 820 units = Rs. 12300 ⇒ 1 units = Rs. 15 ⇒ 441 units = Rs. 6615 ∴ Each installment = Rs. 6615

q: An amount of Rs 6000 lent at 5% per annum compounded interest for 2 years will become = ?

q: The simple interest on a certain sum of money for 3 years at 8% per annum is half the compound interest on Rs. 4000 for 2 years at 10% per annum. The sum placed on simple interest is ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{C}}{\text{.I}}{\text{.}} \\ & {\text{ = Rs}}{\text{.}}\left[ {4000 \times {{\left( {1 + \frac{{10}}{{100}}} \right)}^2} - 4000} \right] \\ & = {\text{ Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {4000 \times \frac{{11}}{{10}} \times \frac{{11}}{{10}} - 4000} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. 840}} \\ & \therefore {\text{Sum = Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {\frac{{420 \times 100}}{{3 \times 8}}} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}1750 \end{aligned}$$

q: There is 60% increase in an amount in 6 years at simple interest. What will be the compound interest of Rs. 12000 after 3 years at the same rate ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let P}} = {\text{Rs}}.100 \\ & {\text{Then,}} \\ & {\text{S}}{\text{.I}}{\text{. = Rs}}.60{\text{ and}} \\ & {\text{T = 6 years}} \\ & {\text{R = }}\frac{{100 \times 60}}{{100 \times 6}}{\text{ = 10\% p}}{\text{.a}}{\text{.}} \\ & {\text{Now}} \\ & {\text{P = Rs 12000,}} \\ & {\text{T = 3 years and}} \\ & {\text{R = 10\% p}}{\text{.a}}{\text{.}} \\ & \therefore {\text{C}}{\text{.I}}{\text{. = Rs}}{\text{.}}\left[ {12000 \times \left\{ {{{\left( {1 + \frac{{10}}{{100}}} \right)}^3} - 1} \right\}} \right] \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {12000 \times \frac{{331}}{{1000}}} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}3972 \end{aligned}$$

q: At what rate percent per annum of compound interest, will a sum of money become four times of itself in two years ?

On a certain sum of money, the difference between the compound interest for a year, payable half yearly, and the simple interest for a year is Rs. 56. If the rate of interest in both the cases is 16%, then the sum is ?

q: On a certain sum of money, the difference between the compound interest for a year payable half yearly, and the simple interest for a year is Rs. 180. If the rate of interest in both the cases is 10%, then the sum is = ?
s: Rate % = 10%, Time = 1 year Case (I) : When interest is calculated yearly, Rate = 10% Case (II) : When interest is calculated half yearly $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow {\text{New rate }}\% = \frac{{10}}{2} = 5\% \\ & {\text{Time = 1}} \times {\text{2}} = {\text{2 years}} \\ & {\text{Effective rate}}\% \\ & {\text{ = 5 + 5 + }}\frac{{5 \times 5}}{{100}} = 10.25\% \\ & {\text{Difference in rates}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {10.25 - 10} \right)\% = 0.25\% \\ & {\text{According to the question,}} \\ & {\text{0}}{\text{.25\% of sum = Rs 180}} \\ & {\text{Sum = }}\frac{{180}}{{0.25}} \times 100 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = {\text{Rs. }}72000 \end{aligned}$$

q: The compound interest accrued on an amount of Rs. 25500 at the end of 3 years is Rs. 8440.50. What would be the simple interest accrued on the same amount at the same rate in the same period ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let the rate be R}}\% {\text{ p}}{\text{.a}}{\text{. }} \\ & {\text{then,}} \\ & {\text{25500}}{\left( {1 + \frac{{\text{R}}}{{100}}} \right)^3} \\ & = 25500 + 8440.50 \\ & = 33940.50 \end{aligned}$$ $$\Rightarrow {\left( {1 + \frac{{\text{R}}}{{100}}} \right)^3} = \frac{{33940.50}}{{25500}} =$$ $$\frac{{1331}}{{1000}} =$$ $${\left( {\frac{{11}}{{10}}} \right)^3}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 1 + \frac{{\text{R}}}{{100}} = \frac{{11}}{{10}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{\text{R}}}{{100}} = \frac{1}{{10}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{R}} = 10\,\% \\ & S.I. = {\text{R}}s.\left( {\frac{{25500 \times 10 \times 3}}{{100}}} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\,7650 \end{aligned}$$

q: The difference between the amount of compound interest and simple interest accrued on an amount of Rs. 26000 at the end of 3 years is Rs. 2994.134. What is the rate of interest p.c.p.a ?
A sum of money becomes eight times in 3 years, If the rate is compounded annually. In how much time will the same amount at the same compound rate become sixteen times ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let principal = P}} \\ & {\bf{Case (I)}} \\ & {\text{Time = 3 years,}} \\ & {\text{Amount = 8P}} \\ & \Rightarrow 8{\text{P = P}}{\left( {1 + \frac{{\text{R}}}{{100}}} \right)^3} \\ & \Rightarrow {\left( 2 \right)^3} = {\left( {1 + \frac{{\text{R}}}{{100}}} \right)^3} \\ & {\text{Taking cube root of both sides,}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{2 = }}\left( {1 + \frac{{\text{R}}}{{100}}} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{R = 100 }}\% \\ & {\bf{Case (II)}} \\ & {\text{Let after t years it will be 16 times}} \\ & \Rightarrow 16{\text{P = P}}{\left( {1 + \frac{{\text{R}}}{{100}}} \right)^{\text{t}}} \\ & \Rightarrow 16 = {\left( 2 \right)^{\text{t}}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\left( 2 \right)^4} = {\left( 2 \right)^{\text{t}}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{t}} = 4 \\ & {\text{Hence required time}} \\ & {\text{(t) = 4 years}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A sum of money placed at compound interest double itself in 4 years. In how many years will it amount to four times itself ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}, \\ & {\text{Principal}} = Rs.\,100\% \\ & {\text{Amount}} = Rs.\,200 \\ & {\text{Rate}} = r\% \\ & {\text{Time}} = 4\,{\text{years}} \\ & {\text{Now}}, \\ & A = P \times {\left[ {1 + \left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right)} \right]^n} \\ & 200 = 100 \times {\left[ {1 + \left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right)} \right]^4} \\ & 2 = {\left[ {1 + \left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right)} \right]^4} - - - - - - \left( i \right) \\ & {\text{If}}\,{\text{sum}}\,{\text{become}}\,{\text{8}}\,{\text{times}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{time}}\,n\,{\text{years}} \\ & {\text{then,}} \\ & 4 = {\left( {1 + \left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right)} \right)^n} \\ & {2^2} = {\left( {1 + \left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right)} \right)^n} - - - - - - \left( {ii} \right) \\ & {\text{Using}}\,{\text{eqn}}\,\left( i \right)in\left( {ii} \right),\,{\text{we}}\,{\text{get}} \\ & {\left( {{{\left[ {1 + \left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right)} \right]}^4}} \right)^2} = {\left( {1 + \left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right)} \right)^n} \\ & {\left[ {1 + \left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right)} \right]^{8}} = {\left( {1 + \left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right)} \right)^n} \\ & {\text{Thus}},\,n = 8\,{\text{years}}. \end{aligned}$$

q: The compound interest on Rs. 30000 at 7% per annum for a certain time is Rs. 4347. The times is = ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Principal = Rs}}{\text{. 30000}} \\ & {\text{CI = Rs 4347}} \\ & {\text{Rate = 7}}\% \\ & {\text{By using formula, }} \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {30000 + 4347} \right) = 30000{\left( {1 + \frac{7}{{100}}} \right)^{\text{t}}} \\ & \Rightarrow 34347 = 30000{\left( {1 + \frac{7}{{100}}} \right)^{\text{t}}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{34347}}{{30000}} = {\left( {\frac{{107}}{{100}}} \right)^{\text{t}}} \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {\frac{{11449}}{{10000}}} \right) = {\left( {\frac{{107}}{{100}}} \right)^{\text{t}}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\left( {\frac{{107}}{{100}}} \right)^2} = {\left( {\frac{{107}}{{100}}} \right)^{\text{t}}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{t}} = 2\,{\text{years}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A money lender borrows money at 4% per annum and pays the interest at the end of the year. He lends it at 6% per annum compound interest compounded half yearly and receives the interest at the end of the year. In this way, he gains Rs. 104.50, a year. The amount of money be borrows, is ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let the sum Rs}}{\text{. }}x{\text{ }} \\ & {\text{Then,}} \\ & {\text{C}}{\text{.I}}{\text{. when compounded half yearly}} \\ & {\text{ = Rs}}{\text{.}}\left[ {x \times {{\left( {1 + \frac{3}{{100}}} \right)}^2} - x} \right] \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {\frac{{10609}}{{10000}}x - x} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {\frac{{609x}}{{10000}}} \right) \\ & {\text{C}}{\text{.I}}{\text{. when compounded yearly}} \\ & {\text{ = Rs}}{\text{.}}\left[ {x \times \left( {1 + \frac{4}{{100}}} \right) - x} \right] \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {\frac{{26x}}{{25}} - x} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\frac{x}{{25}} \\ & \therefore \frac{{609x}}{{10000}} - \frac{x}{{25}} = 104.50 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{209x}}{{10000}} = 104.50 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \left( {\frac{{104.50 \times 10000}}{{209}}} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow x = 5000 \end{aligned}$$

q: The effective annual rate of interest corresponding to a nominal rate of 6% per annum payable half yearly is = ?
s: Amount of Rs. 100 for 1 year when compounded half yearly $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{ = Rs}}{\text{.}}\left[ {100 \times {{\left( {1 + \frac{3}{{100}}} \right)}^2}} \right] \\ & = {\text{Rs}}.106.09 \\ & \therefore {\text{Effective rate}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {106.09 - 100} \right)\% \\ & = 6.09\,\% \end{aligned}$$

q: A sum of Rs. 8000 will amount to Rs. 8820 in 2 years if the interest is calculated every year. The rate of compound interest is = ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Principal = Rs 8000}} \\ & {\text{Amount = Rs 8820}} \\ & {\text{Let Rate = }}R \\ & {\text{Time = 2 years}} \\ & {\text{By using formula, }} \\ & \Rightarrow 8820 = 8000{\left( {1 + \frac{R}{{100}}} \right)^2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{8820}}{{8000}} = {\left( {1 + \frac{R}{{100}}} \right)^2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{441}}{{400}} = {\left( {1 + \frac{R}{{100}}} \right)^2} \\ & {\text{Taking square root of both sides,}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{21}}{{20}} = \left( {1 + \frac{R}{{100}}} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow R = 5\% \end{aligned}$$

q: The compound interest on a certain some of money for 2 years at 10% per annum is Rs 420. The simple interest on the same sum at the same rate and for the same time will be ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Rate = 10}}\% \\ & {\text{Time = 2 years}} \\ & {\text{Effective rate of CI for 2 years}} \\ & {\text{ = 10 + 10 + }}\frac{{10 \times 10}}{{100}} \\ & = 21\% \\ & {\text{Effective rate of SI for 2 years}} \\ & {\text{ = 2}} \times {\text{10 = 20}}\% \\ & {\text{Required SI}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{420}}{{21}} \times {\text{20 = Rs. 400}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A father left a will of Rs. 16400 for his two sons aged 17 and 18 years. They must get equal amount when they are 20 years, at 5% compound interest. Find the present share of the younger son = ?
s: Let the share of the younger and elder sons be Rs. x and Rs. (16400 - x) Then, amount of Rs. x after 3 years = Amount of Rs. (16400 - x) after 2 years $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow x{\left( {1 + \frac{5}{{100}}} \right)^3} = \left( {16400 - x} \right){\left( {1 + \frac{5}{{100}}} \right)^2} \\ & \Rightarrow x\left( {1 + \frac{5}{{100}}} \right) = \left( {16400 - x} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{21x}}{{20}} + x = 16400 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{41x}}{{20}} = 16400 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \left( {\frac{{16400 \times 20}}{{41}}} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow x = 8000 \end{aligned}$$

q: A sum of money put at compound interest amounts in 2 years to Rs. 672 and in 3 years Rs. 714. The rate of interest per annum is = ?
